draft.title: Shrines and rituals
card: A Shinto shrine is a sacred place where people worship and approach the kami. A torii gate often marks the entrance, showing the move from the everyday world into sacred ground.
Worshippers usually begin with purification. At many shrines they rinse their hands and mouth with water at a basin near the entrance.
Worshippers then make offerings, such as money, food or sake, to show respect and thanks to the kami.
Prayers follow. A worshipper may bow, clap and pray at the main hall. Priests also lead prayers and rituals at shrines.
draft.remember: At a shrine, worshippers pass the torii, purify themselves, make offerings and pray.

a.q: What is the main purpose of a torii gate at a Shinto shrine?
opts: It marks the entrance to sacred ground
It holds the offerings left for the kami
It is the place where priests live
It is the basin used to rinse the hands
a.why: A torii gate marks the entrance and shows the move from the everyday world into sacred ground. The water basin is used for purification, but it is a separate feature from the gate.
a.clue: Think about where a worshipper stands before entering the shrine.

b.q: Aiko visits a shrine in Kyoto. She rinses her hands and mouth at the basin, then leaves a small coin. Which two parts of worship has she done?
opts: Purification, then an offering
An offering, then a prayer
A prayer, then purification
Passing the torii, then a prayer
b.why: Rinsing at the basin is purification, and leaving a coin is an offering. She has not yet prayed, so the options that include a prayer are wrong. Passing the torii is not named as something she did.
b.clue: Match each action Aiko does to one of the parts of worship on the card.

a.best: It marks the entrance to sacred ground

problems.detail: The remember line gives a fixed four-step sequence (pass the torii, purify, offer, pray) for every visit. The card hedges these steps with 'often', 'usually' and 'at many shrines', and never presents passing the torii as a step of worship.
